area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a loft, a tower and a kitchen
area.scope.1.why: Condensers on loft and tower roofs mean roof hatches, ladders, and sometimes a crane for a replacement.
area.scope.2.why: High-rises want a certificate of insurance, a booked freight elevator and set working hours before anyone arrives.
area.scope.3.why: Steam and hot-water boilers in converted warehouses, fan coils in towers, forced air in newer mid-rises. Each is a different repair.
area.scope.4.why: Line sets and ductwork can't be hidden in a slab. In a loft they have to run where they look intentional.
area.scope.5.why: Make-up air has to balance the hood. Work is scheduled around service on Randolph and in Fulton Market.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your West Loop building
area.buildings.1.title: Converted warehouse
area.buildings.1.body: Steam or hot-water radiators, or split systems added later. Exposed ceilings decide where ducts go.
area.buildings.2.title: High-rise condo
area.buildings.2.body: In-unit fan coils or air handlers on a building loop. Management approval and elevator booking first.
area.buildings.3.title: Condo or townhome
area.buildings.3.body: Forced-air furnaces with roof or balcony condensers, and newer heat pumps in recent builds.
area.buildings.4.title: Restaurant or office
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units, make-up air and exhaust. Scheduled around service and opening hours.

area.faq.heading: West Loop HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Do I need a new furnace, or can mine be repaired?
area.faq.1.a: Often it can be repaired. We diagnose first, and where the unit has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.faq.2.q: Do you work in West Loop high-rises?
area.faq.3.q: Can you service the steam boiler in my loft?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC repair in Chicago need a permit?
area.cta.body: Have the make of your furnace, boiler or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a high-rise, mention your building's work hours.

extras.faq.2.a: Yes. Before a visit, high-rises usually want a certificate of insurance, a booked freight elevator and set working hours, so we book around your building's elevator and work hours. In towers that's often in-unit fan coils or air handlers on a building loop.
extras.faq.3.a: Yes. We service hot-water and steam boilers in vintage two-flats and converted lofts: pressure, circulators, zone valves and venting.
extras.faq.4.a: No. Chicago doesn't require a permit to repair, diagnose or maintain heating and cooling. Permits cover installs and construction, so a company's permit count says little about its repair work.
extras.faq.5.a: Monday to Friday, 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, and Saturday, 6:00 AM to 3:30 PM. Call (773) 238-3838.
